items.followUp: Draw and label a stomach, then describe its main regions and inner lining.

rubric.why: Checks the stomach’s entrance and its connection to the oesophagus.
rubric.description: Shows the oesophagus entering the stomach at its cardiac end.
rubric.how: Draw and label the oesophagus entering the upper end of the stomach.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the stomach’s regions.
rubric.description: Labels the fundus, body and pyloric region, or identifies the cardiac end.
rubric.how: Label the principal regions on the stomach diagram.

rubric.why: Checks the stomach’s outlet and its connection to the intestine.
rubric.description: Shows the pyloric outlet leading to the duodenum.
rubric.how: Label the pyloric sphincter or the duodenum at the lower outlet.

rubric.why: Checks a feature of the inner lining or stomach wall.
rubric.description: Shows the folded inner lining (rugae) or gastric glands.
rubric.how: Draw and label the folds or gastric glands.

modelAnswer: Draw a J-shaped outline about 8 cm high and 5 cm wide for the stomach.
Draw a 2 cm-long oesophagus entering its upper, cardiac end; label the fundus, body and pyloric region.
Draw a pyloric sphincter at the lower outlet and a 2 cm-long duodenum leading away from it; label both.
Draw folds inside the stomach and label them rugae; label gastric glands in the stomach wall.
The stomach is a muscular sac between the oesophagus and the small intestine; its inner lining has folds and gastric glands.
